notes: REAL, POPULATED DATA FOUND — first result row shape verified for this suite. No query params on this capability are formally required (issue_id/issue_type/priority/compact/include_relations/p/per_page/q are all optional); the contract itself says omitting all filters is a legal, if expensive, account-wide dump. Since the contract also says a project_id can't narrow this endpoint at all (confirmed by attempt #1 — the MCP layer's own allow-list rejects an unknown 'project_id' query key before any HTTP call), I did not need to try the fixture project or the older named projects (Default Project 59544, Demo KB 83363, Test LFI 72632, JD RCA Flaky Samples PR-2002) individually — a single unfiltered call at p=1, compact=false already searches every project in the account's group in one shot. It returned info.count=227467 total results and 30 real rows spanning projects 379335189, 379329553, 379335215, 379335211 (all in the __mcp-capability-fixture__ project family but NOT the fixture project used by this suite's own fixture pool, and NOT the __readonly__/__scratch__ sub-buckets named in this task — these are sibling projects created by other test runs in the same shared account, with genuinely executed cases: statuses 'failed', 'passed', 'blocked' all observed with real timestamps from 2026-09-17). This satisfies the task's ask for a populated row to verify item shape against — UNVERIFIED is no longer warranted for the `result` entity's item shape after this probe. Outcome vocabulary: this capability exposes TWO representations of the same concept and they disagree with each other AND with the sibling write capability. (1) result_status.field_value is display-case ('Failed', 'Passed', 'Blocked') and matches the vocabulary create_test_results_for_test_run documents for its own `status` body field ("Passed", "Failed", "Untested" — display-case names configured per project). (2) result_status.internal_name is lowercase ('failed', 'passed', 'blocked'). (3) the row's own top-level `status` field is declared as a plain string ('Status name', example 'passed') but was null in 29 of 30 rows and, in the one row where it was populated, held the LOWERCASE internal_name token ('blocked') rather than the display-case name search's own result_status.field_value carries for the identical row, or that the write endpoint expects back. So within one response object, `status` and `result_status.field_value` can disagree in casing for the same outcome — a same-entity vocabulary disagreement, and `status` additionally violates its own declared (non-nullable) string type by being null nearly all the time. Pre-created/untested result rows: NOT observed. All 30 sampled rows (real executions across four different projects/runs) carried a genuine result_status of failed/passed/blocked with real created_at/updated_at timestamps; none showed 'untested' or a null result_status. This is consistent with the endpoint being backed by the actual TestResult execution table — a run/case mapping that has never been executed has no TestResult row to be found by this search, so 'a result' here appears to mean a genuine logged execution, not the always-present latest_result_id placeholder every test-run row carries. attachments (declared non-nullable array) was null on every row rather than an array — could not observe a populated attachments array in this sample. Severity: overall LOW-to-MODERATE — the endpoint works, is genuinely populated, and most declared fields matched; the drift is in nested sub-object field lists (result_status, author, issues) and in status/attachments failing to honor their declared (non-nullable) types, plus the status-casing disagreement noted above.
